rejectedSkills.reason: "WordPress Playground Blueprints for declarative environment setup" (per repo README skill table). Environment/CI provisioning tooling, not a design activity.

"Classifies WordPress repos and routes to the right workflow" -- an internal meta-router for this skill collection itself, not a design activity and not independently useful once copied out of the collection.
"Capability-based permissions and REST API authentication" -- backend authorization/API architecture, not design.
"Audit a plugin's REST surface and propose Abilities API registrations" -- backend security/API audit, not a design or UX audit.
"Verify a plugin's Abilities API registrations against declarations" -- backend API conformance checking, not design.

"Gutenberg blocks: block.json, attributes, rendering, deprecations" -- block engineering (schema, PHP/JS rendering, deprecation handling) rather than visual/interaction design decisions; adjacent to design in that it ships block UI, but the skill's own scope is implementation mechanics. Registry budget for this repo (3 vendor slots) was spent on wpds, wp-block-themes and wp-patterns, which are more directly design-centric.

"Frontend interactivity with data-wp-* directives and stores" -- a JavaScript state/directive framework for wiring behavior, not an interaction-design skill about what the behavior should be; adjacent but implementation-focused.

"Profiling, caching, database optimization, Server-Timing" -- backend performance engineering, not design (perceived-performance-as-UX is covered by the registry's existing design-engineering category via other vendored skills, not by this WordPress-specific profiling skill).
"PHPStan static analysis for WordPress projects" -- pure code-quality tooling, not design.
"WordPress Playground routing, CLI runs, browser previews, snapshots" -- dev-environment/CI tooling, not design.
"Plugin architecture, hooks, settings API, security" -- backend plugin engineering, not design.
"WordPress Plugin Directory Guidelines" -- marketplace policy/compliance checklist, not a design activity.

"Detects project type, tooling, and versions automatically" -- a filesystem-detection utility (its script is bundled into the vendored wp-block-themes and wp-patterns manifests as a dependency, per the self-containment rule) with no design content of its own.
"REST API routes/endpoints, schema, auth, and response shaping" -- backend API design (in the software-architecture sense, not product/UX design), not in scope.
"WP-CLI commands, automation, multisite, search-replace" -- ops/automation tooling, not design.

#### WordPress/agent-skills -- non-vendored skills (inspected 2026-08-29, pin d87ee6916e740c7960b6959220c0481a41b320c7)
Scored from the repo's own README skill-description table (each is a one-line, repo-maintained summary of that skill's SKILL.md description) plus the skills/ directory listing, rather than a full per-file read, since the assignment set an explicit budget of at most 3 vendored skills for this repo and instructed staying economical; a deep read was reserved for the 3 candidates that passed the initial relevance screen (wpds, wp-block-themes, wp-patterns -- see their own manifests). All 15 skills here are WordPress backend/platform engineering, dev-ops, or compliance tooling (REST API schemas and auth, capability/Abilities-API permissions and audits, WP-CLI automation, PHPStan static analysis, Playground/Blueprint environment provisioning, plugin directory policy, and an internal project-classification router), scoring relevance 0 per the rubric's explicit rule ("Generic coding/marketing/PM content. Reject regardless of quality"). wp-block-development and wp-interactivity-api are scored relevance 1 (adjacent) since they shape block/frontend UI surfaces even though their own scope is implementation mechanics (block.json/rendering/deprecations; data-wp-* directives and stores) rather than design decisions -- with only 3 vendor slots available for this repo, the budget went to the three skills whose primary subject is a design decision (WPDS component/token usage, theme.json visual styling, block-pattern composition) rather than an engineering API.
